newsitem.title: USA: U.S. airlines boosted by earnings, interest rates.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlines boosted by earnings, interest rates.

text.p: U.S. airlines stocks surged on Thursday, boosted by strong earnings and a favorable downturn in interest rates.

Analysts said better-than-expected earnings from American Airlines parent AMR Corp on Wednesday and Continental Airlines Inc on Thursday supported the view that others in the group will show strong first-quarter profits.
"Airlines continue to do well," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "They are coming up with decent earnings."
Airlines operate with high levels of debt, making them particularly sensitive to fluctuations in interest rates.
On Thursday the 30-year Treasury bond was up 14/32, its yield dropping to 7.06 percent from Wednesday's close at 7.10.
"If you get higher earnings and lower interest rates simultaneously, the (airline) stocks will go through the roof," said Gruntal and Co airline analyst Steven Lewins.
AMR Corp rose 2-3/4 to 87-3/4. It got a boost from a Morgan Stanley analyst who upgraded the stock to strong buy from outperform.

Continental added 3/8 to 32-3/4. United Airlines parent UAL Corp gained 2-3/8 to 75-3/8. Delta Air Lines Inc rose three to 93-7/8, US Airways Group Inc gained one to 27-7/8 and Southwest Airlines Co rose 1-1/4 to 23-5/8.
